I home-schooled my kids through the 8th grade, out of necessity---the local school system where we lived at the time was ranked in the bottom 5% of the state.

We used the k-12 curriculum (k12.com) because it was viewed as a Title 1 school in that state, just like a brick-and-mortar schoolhouse. We received all the books, lab supplies, art supplies, even a computer, printer, and other cool stuff in the mail, all for free. There was an online class with other students and a teacher that we had to do each day for a short time.

I was considered a "learning coach". The kids sat on my knees and we went at it. When I showed them how to fill out a multiplication table, their eyes lit up and they fell in love with learning. I had more than one, so a natural sibling rivalry took place, each trying to outdo the other. We had a blast.

Parents were encouraged to have meet-ups with other k-12 parents. We had group field trips to parks, museums, and other places of interest.

Judeo-Christianity was taught as part of 1st and 2nd grade History class (basically along with the Big Bang, they teach "some people believe in evolution, but some people believe in intelligent design...those people believe that In the beginning, God...") And they also gave some time to buddhism, islam, and hinduism. But since this is happening under your roof, you can guide your children as you wish.

Since it was Title 1, we still had to submit to the yearly state testing. You know...filling in the circles with the number 2 pencils.

It turns out that you can. Slip your document in the food saver sleeve and vacuum seal. You can then run it through the laminator. Aside from extra seal around the entire document, I'm not sure that there's another benefit. Plus, the texture of the food saver sleeve doesn't go away. So if it's not something that you need in perfect, pristine condition, it will work well.
